{"number":1109,"title":"lineage: an unclassified error on the FIRST GET_LINEAGE call aborts the whole Snowflake pull instead of descending","body":"Split out of #892 (per-seed `GET_LINEAGE` traversal), where it got sharper rather than newer.

`SnowflakeLineageProvider._from_get_lineage` classifies the FIRST GET_LINEAGE call's failure through `_reraise_if_feature_unsupported`: an edition gate (`0A000`) or a grant denial becomes `_FeatureUnsupportedError` and the ladder descends to ACCESS_HISTORY / OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES. **Anything else re-raises**, so `fetch_edges` — which only catches `_FeatureUnsupportedError` — propagates it and the entire pull fails, including the floor tier that would have answered fine. This is the pre-#892 probe's behaviour, deliberately left unchanged in that PR and pinned by `test_an_unclassified_failure_on_the_first_call_still_aborts_the_pull`.

Why it matters more now: the probe was ONE trivial call; the traversal is 2xN calls (N = `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_MAX_SEEDS`, default 500). A transient network blip that lands on the first of a thousand calls now costs the whole graph for that refresh, where OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES was sitting right there. Every later seed's failure is already skip-and-count; only the first is fatal.

Note the failure is not silent (the refresh records the error and #1091 surfaces staleness), and the snapshot-prune regime does NOT wipe the cache on an unavailable pull — so this is a lost refresh, not lost data.

Fix shape: treat an unclassified first-call failure the same way the seed-enumeration failure is already treated — skip the tier with a classified reason (`get_lineage: call failed ()`) and let the union answer. The one thing to keep: never fold it into a CONFIDENT EMPTY at the top tier (that would prune the floor's graph); descending is the safe direction.

AC:
- [ ] An unclassified error on the first GET_LINEAGE call descends to the union instead of raising
- [ ] `skipped_tiers` carries a classified reason (exception TYPE, never raw connector text — the #902 rule)
- [ ] The floor's own failure still reports `WarehouseLineageUnavailableError` (a total denial must never read as an empty graph)
- [ ] Regression test with the poison error on call 1 of a multi-seed traversal","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1109","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["enhancement"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-07-28T19:26:54Z","updated_at":"2026-07-28T19:26:54Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1118,"title":"security: connection test paths resolve arbitrary *_secret_name refs from request-supplied config (SSRF + credential exfiltration class)","body":"## Finding (from the /code-review of PR #1116, scored 60 — pre-existing class, filed rather than fixed in-PR)

`_extra_secrets(config, secret_store)` resolves ANY `*_secret_name` field in a connection config against the flat SecretStore namespace and hands the plaintext to `adapter.test()`. Config is user-supplied on the create path and now also on the draft-test path (#1116), and `GET /connections` exposes every connection's config (single-tenant, connection-unscoped by design), so any authenticated user can:

1. Read a victim connection's `catalog_secret_name` off `GET /connections`.
2. `POST /connections/test` (or create+test) with `type=iceberg`, `catalog_uri` pointed at an attacker-controlled host, and the victim's `catalog_secret_name`.
3. The server resolves the victim's real catalog credential and `inject_uri_password()` sends it to the attacker's endpoint — SSRF + credential exfiltration.

The **class is pre-existing** (`test_connection` on a saved row has always resolved `_extra_secrets`, and create accepts arbitrary config at the same auth gate); the draft-test endpoint adds a **trace-less variant** (no persisted row). Under the current single-tenant workspace-trusted model this is an accepted-risk shape, but it becomes a real boundary violation the moment RBAC (#740–#744) introduces users who should NOT be able to wield every stored credential.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide the mitigation: (a) `*_secret_name` in a test/create payload may only reference a secret already attached to a connection the caller may access, or (b) draft-test refuses `*_secret_name` resolution entirely, or (c) explicitly record accepted-risk-until-RBAC with a pointer from ADR 0033.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen covers BOTH the saved-connection test and the draft test.
- [ ] Regression test proving a foreign `*_secret_name` cannot be exfiltrated once mitigated (or the accepted-risk record).

Refs #1116, ADR 0011, ADR 0033 (#740–#744).","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["security"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-01T00:00:24Z","updated_at":"2026-08-01T00:00:24Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1193,"title":"Batch-target resolution preview endpoint (follow-up to #1180)","body":"#1180 added the Single file / Batch pattern mode toggle to `SuiteForm` (#1192), wiring the UI to the backend's existing `resolve_batch`/`BatchSpec` batch-target support (prefix/pattern/strategy/batch).

The AC for #1180 mentioned "the same preview the backend batch resolution gives," but no cheap preview path exists today: `POST /suites/{id}/profile`, `GET /suites/{id}/columns`, and `POST /suites/{id}/column-policy/suggest` all accept only a literal `path`/`table` — none take `pattern`/`strategy`/`batch`/`prefix`. Per #1180's own scoping instruction, #1192 did not add a new backend endpoint to manufacture a preview, and instead only shows the *configured* prefix+pattern+strategy (via `summarizeTarget`), not a resolved file.

**Proposal:** a small endpoint (new route, or a query-param extension of an existing one) that runs `resolve_batch` (backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py) against the connection's live object listing for a given prefix/pattern/strategy/batch and returns the matched file path (or a `BatchNotFoundError`/422 if nothing matches) — surfaced in the suite form as a "resolves to: ``" hint next to the batch fields, giving authors the same confidence a literal-path suite already has before they save.

Not blocking: the client-side validation in `assembleTarget`/`hasCaptureGroup` (mirroring `_batch_spec`'s own rules) plus the backend's authoritative 422 on save already keep a misconfigured batch target from silently going unrunnable.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1193","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["enhancement"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T06:33:35Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T06:33:35Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1195,"title":"Stale TargetKind header comment: says six datasource types / three input shapes","body":"Found in self-review of #1192 (batch-target UI, #1180) — pre-existing, unrelated to that PR's diff, so filing separately rather than bundling into its commit (CLAUDE.md §11: don't batch unrelated changes into one commit).

`frontend/src/components/suites/suiteTarget.ts`, the `TargetKind` header comment:

```
/**
 * A suite's run target (#215) is datasource-shaped: SQL warehouses identify a
 * `table` (+ optional `schema`), Unity Catalog adds a required `catalog`, and
 * flat-file stores (ADLS / S3) identify a `path` (+ optional `file_format`).
 * `targetKind` collapses the six datasource types to the three input shapes the
 * editor renders; orchestration types never reach here (they can't back a suite).
 */
export type TargetKind = 'sql' | 'uc' | 'flatfile' | 'iceberg';
```

This is stale on both counts:
- CLAUDE.md §1 documents **five** datasources (Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, AWS S3, Unity Catalog, Iceberg), not six.
- `TargetKind` itself has **four** members (`'sql' | 'uc' | 'flatfile' | 'iceberg'`), not three, and the prose never mentions Iceberg's `namespace.table` shape at all — it reads as if it predates the Iceberg datasource (#716/#722, ADR 0030).

Fix: update the comment's counts and add a line covering Iceberg's shape, consistent with how the Unity Catalog and flat-file shapes are each called out.

Not urgent/blocking — it's a doc-comment accuracy issue, not a behavioral bug — but per CLAUDE.md §11 every finding ends fixed or filed, never silently dropped.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1195","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["enhancement"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T06:52:24Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T06:52:25Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1196,"title":"gx_runner: unexpected_index_list is uncapped at capture time on pandas-backed datasources (flat-file/Iceberg)","body":"## What

`backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py` always calls GX with `result_format="COMPLETE"` (lines 278, 286, 295). GX's `partial_unexpected_list` stays capped (~20 rows, `partial_unexpected_count`) on every execution engine, and the SQLAlchemy-backed engines (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) keep `unexpected_index_list` capped too — but under `COMPLETE` format, GX's **pandas** execution engine (used for flat-file/ADLS/S3 and Iceberg-via-`pyiceberg` datasources) returns `unexpected_index_list` **full and untruncated**: every failing row's identifier + value, with no upper bound.

`_extract_sample_failures` (`gx_runner.py:105-113`) copies this list into `sample_failures` verbatim — no slicing/limit anywhere in `gx_runner.py` or `run_service.py`. So a flat-file or Iceberg check with many failing rows (e.g. thousands out of a large table) persists a `sample_failures` JSONB blob of proportional size into the `results` table, and that same size travels over the `GET /runs/{id}` API response.

## Where found

Found during review of #1190 (frontend fix for #1183 — the run-detail failing-rows table). #1190 fixed the *display*-side symptom (the frontend now caps what it renders to 20 rows regardless of source-list size), but the *capture*-side issue — the backend persisting/serving an unbounded list in the first place — is separate, pre-existing (present since `unexpected_index_list` capture landed for #415), and out of that PR's frontend-only scope.

## Why it matters

- **Storage bloat**: `results.sample_failures` JSONB grows unbounded per check run for large pandas-backed failures, with no corresponding value beyond what a ~20-row sample already gives.
- **API payload size**: `GET /runs/{id}` now ships that same unbounded blob to every reader.
- Not a PII/security issue — cells are still correctly redacted per column (`run_service.redact_sample_failures`) — this is a resource/cost concern, not a data-exposure one.

## Suggested fix

Cap `unexpected_index_list` at capture time in `gx_runner._extract_sample_failures` (e.g. slice to the same ~20-row cap `partial_unexpected_count` already gives elsewhere), so the persisted/served sample never has unbounded-list values, instead of leaving the entire safeguard to be display-side and per-consumer.

## Evidence

- `backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py:278,286,295` — `result_format="COMPLETE"` in every run call.
- `backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py:105-113` — `_extract_sample_failures` copies `result[key]` verbatim, no truncation.
- No `.slice()`/length limit found anywhere in `gx_runner.py` or `run_service.py` on `unexpected_index_list`.
- GX (installed, 1.17.2) pandas execution engine: `unexpected_index_list` under `result_format=COMPLETE` is not truncated the way `partial_unexpected_list`/the SQLAlchemy-backed index-list path are.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1196","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug","priority/P2"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T06:53:29Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T06:53:29Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1197,"title":"run_service: redaction label can undercount vs. what's actually rendered when unexpected_index_list and partial_unexpected_list disagree","body":"## What

`backend/app/services/run_service.py`'s `_RedactionTracker` OR-accumulates a column's "was it shown" state across **both** `unexpected_index_list` and `partial_unexpected_list` when a single `sample_failures` payload carries both (`_RedactionTracker.record()`: `column_state[column] = column_state.get(column, False) or shown`, called from both branches inside `redact_sample_failures`).

Each list's per-column show/mask verdict comes from `_known_sensitive`/`classify_column` (`backend/app/services/column_classification.py`), a **value-based heuristic** (ratio of email-shaped/encoded/id-shaped values in whatever sample it's given: `_value_signal`). The two lists are classified against **different value samples** — `unexpected_index_list`'s own rows (`index_vbc = _values_by_column(index_rows)`) vs. `partial_unexpected_list`'s own values — so the *same column name*, including the tested column itself, can legitimately classify as "shown" against one list's sample and "masked" against the other's.

Because the tracker ORs to "shown" if *either* list shows a column, a column that is masked in `unexpected_index_list` but classified as shown in `partial_unexpected_list` ends up excluded from `redacted_columns` / undercounted in the `redaction` summary state — even though every cell for that column in `unexpected_index_list` (now the list the frontend renders, per #1190) reads `""`.

## Why it's not a security bug

This is a **display-honesty undercount only**, not a PII leak: whichever list is actually rendered has its own cells correctly masked according to that list's own classification. The label text (`redaction` / `redactedColumns`, surfaced next to the sample table as "N columns redacted" / "values redacted" / "values shown") can merely *understate* how much masking happened relative to what's on screen — it can never overstate it (a genuinely shown value always sets `shown=True` in the tracker, so a shown cell is never mislabeled as redacted).

## Where found

Found during review of #1190 (frontend fix for #1183, which changes `RunDetail.tsx` to prefer rendering `unexpected_index_list` over `partial_unexpected_list`). This backend behavior pre-dates #1190 — #1190 doesn't touch `run_service.py` at all — but #1190's frontend change makes the divergence newly *visible*: before it, the frontend only ever rendered `partial_unexpected_list`, and the tracker's OR-toward-"shown" bias happened to be safe because that was the one list on screen.

This reopens the display-honesty bug class #424/#1115 fixed (the redaction label must match what a viewer actually sees).

## Suggested fix

Since the redaction state is already computed **read-time** (#1115 — so a backend fix retroactively corrects the label for old rows, no backfill needed), make `redact_sample_failures`/`_RedactionTracker` classify/track against the **same list the frontend will display**, using the same preference rule #1190 uses on the frontend: a dict-shaped `unexpected_index_list` present → track only from that list; otherwise track from `partial_unexpected_list` (keeping the existing #1115 anonymous-mask semantics for the scalar-list path). Add a regression test with a dual-list sample where the tested column masks in the index list but shows in the partial list, asserting the label reflects the **displayed** (index) list — plus keep the existing #1115 regression tests green.

## Evidence

- `backend/app/services/run_service.py` — `_RedactionTracker.record()` (OR-accumulation), `redact_sample_failures` (processes both `unexpected_index_list` and `partial_unexpected_list` keys into the same tracker).
- `backend/app/services/column_classification.py:314-335` (`_value_signal`) — ratio-based over whatever sample it's given.
- `backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py:28-38` (`_SAMPLE_KEYS`) — both keys can co-occur in one `sample_failures` payload.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1197","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug","priority/P3"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T06:53:48Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T06:53:48Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1199,"title":"Surface trigger-binding env near-miss signals in the product, not just the DB","body":"## Context

#1186 (fixed in #1194) added an ingest-time near-miss signal: when a succeeded pipeline/DAG run matches an ENABLED `trigger_binding` on `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)` but not on `env`, `orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses` now emits a `trigger_binding_env_near_miss` structlog warning **and** upserts a deduped row in `workspace_health` (key `trigger_env_near_miss:`), so the DB retains "this mismatch is still happening" past log retention.

## The gap

That `workspace_health` row is currently **write-only** — no API route and no frontend surface reads it. The only way to see it today is `psql`. This repeats the exact shape #828/#837/#1100 exist to prevent: a signal that's technically recorded but invisible in the product. The Suite Triggers panel (`TriggersPanel.tsx`) only surfaces the #1186 *creation-time* ambiguity warning (`TriggerBindingRead.warnings`) — it has no way to show that an *already-created* binding has a live, ongoing env mismatch.

## Acceptance ideas (pick at design time)

1. A read endpoint (e.g. `GET /admin/orchestration/near-misses` or folded into an existing admin/health surface) that lists current near-miss rows, decoded back to `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, run_env, binding_env, updated_at)` — note the stored `workspace_health.key` is a hash (chosen to fit the 64-char column against Airflow's up-to-256-char DAG ids), so either the row needs a sibling detail column/table, or the read path needs to re-derive candidates by re-running the same query `_record_env_near_misses` uses, filtered to `updated_at` recency.
2. Surface a badge/alert on the Suite Triggers panel for a binding whose `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)` has a recent near-miss row in a DIFFERENT env than the binding itself.
3. Or fold into a future workspace-health/admin dashboard alongside the existing poll-staleness signal (`workspace_health_service.POLL_STALENESS_KEY`).

Scope note: this is a genuine product gap, not a defect in #1194 — the creation-time warning (option 1 from #1186) already covers the "about to create a bad binding" case; this is about an *existing* binding that's silently dead today with no way to discover it short of reading logs or the raw table.

Filed per review of #1194 (git-history reviewer pass) — the review's own words: "the ingest-time signal is invisible except via psql — contradicting workspace_health's purpose (#828/#837/#1100: product-visible, not log-visible)."","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1199","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["enhancement","priority/P3"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T13:19:45Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T13:19:46Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1200,"title":"Non-hermetic test: test_seed_otp_operator_share reads the ambient DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL and fails on a configured dev machine","body":"Found while running the full backend suite for #1179 with the local stack's `.env` sourced (which is how `scripts/test-backend.sh` runs it).

`backend/tests/db/test_seed_otp_operator_share.py::test_a_domain_only_allowlist_targets_nobody` takes no `monkeypatch` and constructs `Settings(**_MAILER, auth_otp_allowed_domains="acme.io")`, asserting `_otp_operator_emails(settings) == []`. But `_otp_operator_emails` falls back to the `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` compose switch, and that variable is set in the gitignored `.env` that `scripts/setup.sh` generates for every local stack (#1150 made OTP the local default, so it is set on any machine that has run setup). With it exported, the call returns that address and the test fails:

```
FAILED backend/tests/db/test_seed_otp_operator_share.py::test_a_domain_only_allowlist_targets_nobody
```

Unsetting `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` makes it pass; nothing else in the suite is affected (3630 passed).

CI is green because CI never sets the variable — so this is invisible there and only bites a developer whose environment is *correctly* configured, which is the worst way round. Its sibling tests in the same file already `monkeypatch.delenv`/`setenv` for exactly this reason; this one and `test_the_allowlist_wins_over_the_switch`'s neighbours should be audited together.

**Fix:** make the test hermetic — `monkeypatch.delenv("DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL", raising=False)`, or better, an autouse fixture in that module so no future test in it can inherit ambient OTP config. Worth a sweep for other `Settings()` constructions in tests that read ambient env.

Not caused by #1179 and not fixed there (unrelated area, one-functionality-per-commit) — filed per the fix-or-file rule.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1200","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T13:26:33Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T13:26:33Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

`backend/tests/db/test_seed_otp_operator_share.py::test_a_domain_only_allowlist_targets_nobody` takes no `monkeypatch` and constructs `Settings(**_MAILER, auth_otp_allowed_domains="acme.io")`, asserting `_otp_operator_emails(settings) == []`. But `_otp_operator_emails` falls back to the `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` compose switch, and that variable is set in the gitignored `.env` that `scripts/setup.sh` generates for every local stack (#1150 made OTP the local default, so it is set on any machine that has run setup). With it exported, the call returns that address and the test fails:

```
FAILED backend/tests/db/test_seed_otp_operator_share.py::test_a_domain_only_allowlist_targets_nobody
```

Unsetting `DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL` makes it pass; nothing else in the suite is affected (3630 passed).

CI is green because CI never sets the variable — so this is invisible there and only bites a developer whose environment is *correctly* configured, which is the worst way round. Its sibling tests in the same file already `monkeypatch.delenv`/`setenv` for exactly this reason; this one and `test_the_allowlist_wins_over_the_switch`'s neighbours should be audited together.

**Fix:** make the test hermetic — `monkeypatch.delenv("DATAQ_SIGNIN_EMAIL", raising=False)`, or better, an autouse fixture in that module so no future test in it can inherit ambient OTP config. Worth a sweep for other `Settings()` constructions in tests that read ambient env.

{"number":1202,"title":"Custom-SQL checks store the unexpected row count only in JSONB observed_value — no metric_value, so no trend or anomaly baseline","body":"Split out of #1179 review so the deferral has a ticket rather than living in prose.

A custom-SQL check (ADR 0019) produces a genuine scalar — the number of unexpected rows — and it lands **only** in JSONB: `observed_value = {"observed_value": 74}` (verified in the #1179 live run against `dataq_retail.gold.feedback_sentiment`). `metric_value` stays NULL on both Snowflake and Unity Catalog.

That is what ADR 0019 §4 decided ("`UnexpectedRowsExpectation` emits an unexpected **row count**, not an unexpected-percent, so `severity.extract_metric` finds no bandable metric and the check resolves binary `pass`/`fail`… Banding severity on the row count is a deferred enhancement"), and the binary behaviour is correct for "this query should return no rows". So this is not a bug.

But it sits against CLAUDE.md §10: *"`metric_value` is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; **don't store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`** (you can't `AVG()`/`STDDEV()` it for trends or anomaly baselines)."* The concrete cost today:

- the per-check metric trend view (#594) has nothing to plot for a custom-SQL check;
- an `anomaly` monitor cannot baseline against it;
- "is this rule getting worse?" is unanswerable in SQL — you would have to unpack JSONB across runs.

**Scope when picked up:**
- Populate `metric_value` from the unexpected row count in `gx_runner`/`severity.extract_metric` for `unexpected_rows_expectation`, on **both** datasources at once — a per-datasource divergence here would make the same check band differently depending on where it runs.
- Decide the semantic deliberately: a raw count is not comparable across tables of different sizes, so consider whether the bandable quantity should be the count or a percentage of the batch (which would cost a second aggregate). ADR 0019 §Consequences already notes this is "an additive change in `severity.extract_metric`, no schema change".
- Existing rows keep NULL; do not backfill a guess.

Thresholds are already optional, so adding a metric must not turn today's binary checks into something that bands unexpectedly — a check with no thresholds must keep resolving exactly as it does now.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1202","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["enhancement"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T13:37:36Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T13:37:36Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":1203,"title":"A GX SQL-batch exception message can carry target CELL data into results.observed_value, outside the column policy","body":"Found during the #1179 review (PR #1201). Pre-existing on Snowflake, newly reachable on Unity Catalog now that custom SQL runs there — filed rather than folded in, since the fix belongs in the shared `gx_runner`/`run_service` path, not in one datasource.

`backend/app/services/run_service.py` `_build_result` routes an errored check like this:

```python
if outcome.errored:
    # An errored check has no observed metric and no failing-row sample; surface
    # the (schema-level, row-data-free) GX message for debugging instead.
    observed = {"error": outcome.error_message} if outcome.error_message else None
```

The parenthetical is the assumption at issue. `outcome.error_message` is GX's `exception_info.exception_message`, passed through verbatim by `gx_runner.to_suite_outcome`. On a **SQL execution engine** that is typically a SQLAlchemy `StatementError`, whose `str()` appends the statement and its bound parameters:

```
(databricks.sql.exc.ServerOperationError) ...
[SQL: SELECT ... FROM ...]
[parameters: (...)]
```

and a warehouse cast/conversion error commonly **quotes the offending cell value** in its own message (`Cannot parse '' as INT`, etc.).

That lands in `results.observed_value`, which:
- is **not** the `sample_failures` path, so it is outside the retention sweep and outside the suite's column-redaction policy;
- reaches the run-detail API, the UI, alerts and MCP output unredacted.

This is the same shape #989 fixed for monitors, where a cell value was moved out of the message and onto a structured field precisely so the read layer could redact it. The GX path never got that treatment.

**Reachability:** any custom-SQL check (ADR 0019) or column expectation whose evaluation raises inside a SQL engine. Snowflake has had this since ADR 0019; UC joins it with #1179. The flat-file/pandas runners are less exposed (no SQL echo) but a pandas exception can also quote a value.

**Suggested fix** (needs a design decision, hence a ticket not a patch):
1. Classify or scrub the GX `exception_message` before it reaches `observed_value` — but note the message is genuinely the most actionable diagnostic a user gets for a broken query, so a blanket `classify_failure_reason` would regress usability the way it would have for `MonitorConfigError` (see `SafeMonitorError`'s docstring for why that distinction was drawn).
2. More likely the right shape: strip the `[SQL: …] [parameters: …]` tail (SQLAlchemy exposes `.statement`/`.params` separately, so this is structural, not regex-on-prose), keep the driver's own first line, and put anything value-bearing on a structured field that passes through the column policy — the #989 pattern.
3. Add a regression test that a `StatementError` carrying a parameter value does not appear in the persisted `observed_value`.

Not blocking #1179: that PR leaves the behaviour exactly as Snowflake already had it, and deliberately did not introduce a UC-only divergence.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1203","user":{"login":"TheurgicDuke771","id":25581767,"profile_url":"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/25581767?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["bug"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-08T13:42:11Z","updated_at":"2026-08-08T13:42:11Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

I've pulled all 19 open issues numbered above 1000 and read every one in full. Here's the triage:

**Excluded from "fix now" (3 issues):**
- **#1118** (SSRF/credential-exfil via `*_secret_name`) — the issue text itself says this is an accepted-risk shape under the current single-tenant model that only becomes a real boundary violation once RBAC (#740–#744) ships. Needs that design decision first, not a patch.
- **#1030, #1032** (harness: dbt GRANT hook, deployed Airflow/dbt still inject `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD`) — these require a Snowsight GRANT and a Terraform apply against live (currently-stopped) harness infra. Per standing practice, harness Terraform applies aren't done unplanned.

**16 issues are genuinely fixable in this repo right now.** Ranked by priority/dependency:

| Tier | Issues | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **1 — quick wins** | #1195 (stale doc comment), #1200 (non-hermetic test), #1102 (missing `connect_timeout`) | Trivial, zero dependencies, low risk |
| **2 — security/data-integrity** | #1203 (SQL exception leaks cell data into `observed_value`, bypassing column redaction), #1196 (`unexpected_index_list` uncapped — storage/API bloat), #1197 (redaction label undercounts vs. displayed list) | #1196/#1197/#1203 all touch `gx_runner.py`/`run_service.py` — same-file, so must be sequential, not parallel. #1203 is the sharpest (redaction-policy bypass) despite carrying no P-label |
| **3 — backend bugs, well-scoped** | #1101 (phantom "delivered" stamp on health alerts), #1109 (lineage first-call error kills whole pull), #1104 (inventory sync fails invisibly — needs a quick check on whether it needs a migration) | Independent files, can parallelize |
| **4 — API/frontend consistency** | #1108 (paging totals), #1107 (tree-view abort-on-unmount), #1205 (suite detail missing batch-target summary) | Independent, can parallelize |
| **5 — larger/design-gated** | #1001 (profiler sampler), #1193 (batch-target preview endpoint), #1199 (surface near-miss signal in product), #1202 (custom-SQL `metric_value` — needs a count-vs-percentage decision) | Each is a small feature, not a one-line fix |

Given CLAUDE.md's one-functionality-per-commit + code-review-per-PR discipline, that's potentially ~16 separate PRs — too much to respond after the fact. Let me confirm scope before I start opening branches/PRs.

input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ), a data-quality platform. Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first — it defines the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge) and the working agreements. Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1195. Run `gh issue view 1195` for the full text, but in short: `frontend/src/components/suites/suiteTarget.ts`'s `TargetKind` header comment is stale — it says "six datasource types" (should be five, per CLAUDE.md §1: Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog, Iceberg) and "three input shapes" (the type itself has four members: 'sql' | 'uc' | 'flatfile' | 'iceberg'), and never mentions Iceberg's `namespace.table` shape. Fix: correct the counts and add a line describing Iceberg's shape, consistent with how UC and flat-file are each called out.

Workflow:
1. `git checkout -b fix/issue-1195-stale-targetkind-comment` (you're already in an isolated worktree, base off main/origin main).
2. Fix the comment only — this is a pure doc-comment change, no behavior change, no test needed.
3. Run frontend lint/format (prettier/eslint) on the touched file to confirm no issues: check `frontend/package.json` scripts.

input.description: Fix #1102 missing connect_timeout
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1102. Run `gh issue view 1102` for full text. In short: `backend/app/db/session.py` sets `lock_timeout=5000ms` on the engine but no `connect_timeout` — if the DB is fully unreachable (network partition), any `get_session()` caller blocks on the initial TCP connect for OS/driver defaults (can be minutes), which also delays graceful API shutdown (the #1052 staleness loop awaits its task during lifespan shutdown). input.description: Fix #1196/#1197/#1203 gx_runner+run_service cluster
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ), a data-quality platform built on Great Expectations. Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root FIRST — it defines the mandatory per-functionality workflow (one branch/PR per functionality, tests, /code-review skill, push, PR, merge) and critical rules (never store metrics only in JSONB, redaction happens at the logger/read layer, PII redaction is load-bearing). Follow it exactly. This is a higher-stakes cluster (touches the redaction/security-adjacent path), so be careful and precise.

You have THREE related GitHub issues to fix, in this exact order, as three SEPARATE PRs, each fully merged before you start the next (so each PR's diff is clean and reviewable on its own, and so you're always branching from up-to-date main):

## 1. Issue #1196 (run first) — cap unexpected_index_list at capture time
Run `gh issue view 1196` for full text. Summary: `backend/app/datasources/gx_runner.py` calls GX with `result_format="COMPLETE"` everywhere (around lines 278, 286, 295). On the pandas execution engine (flat-file/ADLS/S3/Iceberg datasources), GX's `unexpected_index_list` comes back FULLY UNTRUNCATED under COMPLETE format (unlike the SQLAlchemy-backed engines, and unlike `partial_unexpected_list` which stays capped at ~20 rows / `partial_unexpected_count`). `_extract_sample_failures` (gx_runner.py:105-113) copies this list into `sample_failures` verbatim with no slicing anywhere in gx_runner.py or run_service.py. This means unbounded JSONB storage growth and unbounded API response size for `GET /runs/{id}` on large pandas-backed failures.
Fix: cap `unexpected_index_list` at capture time in `gx_runner._extract_sample_failures`, slicing to the same ~20-row cap `partial_unexpected_count` already gives elsewhere. Add a test asserting the captured list is bounded even when GX returns thousands of entries (pandas-backed fixture with a large failure count).

## 2. Issue #1197 (run second, after #1196 is merged and you've rebased) — redaction label undercount
Run `gh issue view 1197` for full text. Summary: `backend/app/services/run_service.py`'s `_RedactionTracker.record()` OR-accumulates a column's "was it shown" state across BOTH `unexpected_index_list` and `partial_unexpected_list` when both are present in one `sample_failures` payload. Each list is classified independently via `_known_sensitive`/`classify_column` (backend/app/services/column_classification.py, value-based heuristic over each list's OWN sample) — so the same column can classify "shown" against one list and "masked" against the other. Because the tracker ORs toward "shown", a column masked in `unexpected_index_list` (the list the frontend actually renders now, per already-merged PR #1190) but classified shown in `partial_unexpected_list` gets excluded from `redacted_columns` / undercounted in the `redaction` summary — even though every cell for that column in the DISPLAYED list reads "∎∎∎". This is a display-honesty bug (not a PII leak — whichever list is rendered has its own cells correctly masked), reopening the class #424/#1115 fixed.
Fix: since redaction state is computed read-time (#1115), make `redact_sample_failures`/`_RedactionTracker` classify/track against the SAME list the frontend displays: if a dict-shaped `unexpected_index_list` is present, track only from that list; otherwise track from `partial_unexpected_list` (keep existing #1115 anonymous-mask semantics for the scalar-list path). Add a regression test with a dual-list sample where the tested column masks in the index list but shows in the partial list — assert the label reflects the DISPLAYED (index) list. Keep the existing #1115 regression tests green.

## 3. Issue #1203 (run third, after #1197 is merged and you've rebased) — SQL exception leaks cell data into observed_value
Run `gh issue view 1203` for full text. Summary: `backend/app/services/run_service.py::_build_result` does `observed = {"error": outcome.error_message} if outcome.error_message else None` for an errored check. `outcome.error_message` is GX's `exception_info.exception_message` passed through verbatim. On a SQL execution engine (Snowflake, and now Unity Catalog via #1179), that's typically a SQLAlchemy `StatementError`, whose `str()` appends `[SQL: ...] [parameters: (...)]` — and warehouse cast/conversion errors commonly quote the offending CELL VALUE in the message itself (e.g. "Cannot parse '<value>' as INT"). This lands in `results.observed_value`, which is OUTSIDE the sample_failures retention sweep and OUTSIDE the suite's column-redaction policy — it reaches the run-detail API, UI, alerts, and MCP output completely unredacted. This is the same shape #989 already fixed for monitors (moving a cell value out of the message onto a structured field the read layer can redact).
Fix direction (per the issue, a design decision but with a clear suggested shape): strip the `[SQL: …] [parameters: …]` tail structurally — SQLAlchemy exposes `.statement`/`.params` separately on `StatementError`, so this is a structural strip (check `orig`/`statement`/`params` attributes), NOT a regex-on-prose hack — keep the driver's own first line of the message. Do NOT apply a blanket `classify_failure_reason`-style scrub (the issue explicitly warns this would regress usability — the message is often the most actionable diagnostic a user gets for a broken query; see `SafeMonitorError`'s docstring for why that distinction was drawn). Add a regression test: construct/simulate a `StatementError` carrying a parameter value, run it through `_build_result`, and assert the persisted `observed_value` does NOT contain that parameter value or the `[SQL:`/`[parameters:` tail, but DOES retain the driver's first-line message. This must work identically for both Snowflake and Unity Catalog (shared gx_runner/run_service path — no per-datasource divergence).

Workflow (repeat for EACH of the three, in order):
1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run` — it swallows stdin and fakes broken verdicts on this repo's tests).
2. `git checkout main && git pull` then `git checkout -b fix/issue-<N>-<slug>` off up-to-date main.
3. Implement the fix + tests as specified above.
4. Run Black/Ruff/mypy + the full affected test files locally (not just your new test) — confirm nothing else broke, especially the existing #1115/#989/#1190 regression tests mentioned above.
5. Commit (conventional commit, `Fixes #<N>`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push, open PR (use `.github/pull_request_template.md`), milestone matching that issue's own milestone (`gh issue view <N> --json milestone`).
6. Run the `/code-review` skill (Skill tool, skill "code-review") on your diff — this cluster touches the redaction/security-sensitive path so take findings seriously. Fix blocking findings in a follow-up commit and push again. File a new GitHub issue for anything genuinely deferred (never drop silently, per CLAUDE.md's fixed-or-filed rule) — note in the PR/issue that it's a follow-up from this cluster.
7. Wait for CI green (`gh pr checks --watch`). Only squash-merge (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`) if CI is green AND the code-review found nothing blocking. If code-review or CI surfaces something you're not confident fixing correctly, leave the PR open and say so clearly in your final report rather than merging something shaky — this path is security-adjacent.
8. Only THEN move to the next issue in the list.

At the end, report: for each of the 3 issues — PR URL, merge status (merged / open-and-why), and any follow-up issues filed. Be explicit about the #1197 and #1203 fixes' correctness reasoning since they're the trickiest.

Gotchas: shell may be fish (quote glob flags, no `timeout` binary — don't use it). Never `--no-verify`, never force-push. Don't drop a finding silently — every review finding ends fixed or filed.

1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run` — it swallows stdin and fakes broken verdicts on this repo's tests).
2. `git checkout main && git pull` then `git checkout -b fix/issue-<N>-<slug>` off up-to-date main.

input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1101. Summary: `publish_connection_health` in `backend/app/worker/tasks.py` sets `connections.health_alerted_at` whenever `CompositePublisher.publish_health` returns without raising. Apply the identical contract to `publish_health`: the per-connection path claims the flag with a conditional UPDATE BEFORE dispatching the send task (per #842/#843) — so your fix belongs in `publish_connection_health`'s post-publish bookkeeping: release the claim on an undeliverable publish, mirroring the existing publish-failed path. Write tests specifically around the #842 claim/release flow (a workspace with zero configured channels must NOT stamp `health_alerted_at`; a workspace with a configured channel that actually sends must still stamp it).

1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run`).

input.description: Fix #1109 lineage first-call abort
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1109. Run `gh issue view 1109` for full text. Summary: `SnowflakeLineageProvider._from_get_lineage` classifies the FIRST `GET_LINEAGE` call's failure through `_reraise_if_feature_unsupported`: an edition gate (`0A000`) or grant denial becomes `_FeatureUnsupportedError` and the tier ladder descends to ACCESS_HISTORY / OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES. Anything else re-raises, and since `fetch_edges` only catches `_FeatureUnsupportedError`, the WHOLE pull fails — including lower tiers that would have answered fine. This behavior is deliberate/pinned for the pre-existing single-probe case (test `test_an_unclassified_failure_on_the_first_call_still_aborts_the_pull` exists and encodes it), but the per-seed traversal (#892) now makes up to 2×N calls (N = `WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_MAX_SEEDS`, default 500) — so a transient blip on call 1 of 1000 now costs the entire graph.

Fix shape (per the issue): treat an unclassified first-call failure the same way seed-enumeration failures are already treated — skip that tier with a classified reason (e.g. `"get_lineage: call failed: <ExceptionType>"`) and let the union of remaining tiers answer, instead of raising. Critical constraint: do NOT fold this into a CONFIDENT EMPTY at the top tier (that would incorrectly prune a lower tier's real graph) — descending must be the only effect. Also critical: the FLOOR tier's own total failure must still raise `WarehouseLineageUnavailableError` — a total denial must never silently read as an empty graph. The classified reason must carry the exception TYPE only, never raw connector text (the #902 rule — check that rule before writing the reason string).

Required test: a regression test with a poison/unclassified error injected on call 1 of a multi-seed traversal, asserting it descends to the union instead of raising, and that `skipped_tiers` carries the classified reason. Also update/replace the existing pinned test `test_an_unclassified_failure_on_the_first_call_still_aborts_the_pull` since its asserted behavior is exactly what you're changing — rename/rewrite it to assert the NEW (descend, not abort) behavior, and note in your commit why the old pin is being flipped.

Workflow:
1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run`).
2. Branch: `git checkout -b fix/issue-1109-lineage-first-call-abort`.
3. Implement + tests as above. Find the relevant lineage provider file (search for `_from_get_lineage`, `_reraise_if_feature_unsupported`, `fetch_edges` under `backend/app/`).
4. Run Black/Ruff/mypy + the full lineage test suite locally (not just your new test).

input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge), AND note CLAUDE.md's rule: "Backward-compatible migrations only. No DROP COLUMN + code change in same PR. Two-step deploys from W5 onward." Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1104. Run `gh issue view 1104` for full text. Summary: a connection with `inventory_sync: true` whose principal can't read the catalog (UC: PAT lacks SELECT on `system.information_schema`; Snowflake: revoked INFORMATION_SCHEMA access) fails every daily tick inside `sync_connection_inventory`, caught fail-soft and logged (`inventory_sync_connection_failed`) — correct for the sweep, but the user sees: toggle on, connection test green (the `SELECT 1` probe doesn't exercise this query), zero assets ever appear, no surface says why. This is the #828 shape (a feature the UI reports enabled while it silently does nothing).

Fix direction from the issue: "record the last sync outcome per connection (reuse the `lineage_last_error`-style columns pattern or a config-adjacent state) and surface it where the toggle lives (connection detail) — 'inventory sync failing since <ts>: <reason>'. Classify the grant error specifically (the UC error names the schema)."

IMPORTANT — decide the storage mechanism carefully before implementing: look at how `lineage_last_error` is actually stored on the connections model (grep `backend/app/db/models.py` or equivalent) to see if it's a plain nullable column already added via a prior migration — if so, check whether adding a sibling `inventory_sync_last_error`/`inventory_sync_failing_since` column is the intended pattern (a new nullable column addition IS backward-compatible — adding a nullable column is safe in one PR, unlike dropping one). Alternatively check issue #1199's approach (`workspace_health` table with a hashed key) as a migration-free alternative if you'd rather avoid a schema change — read `gh issue view 1199` for that pattern. Pick whichever fits the existing codebase convention better; a migration is fine here (it's additive/nullable, not a drop), just make sure it's genuinely backward-compatible and follows the existing Alembic revision-id conventions (check `backend/alembic/versions/` for the current head and generate a proper new revision — collisions have happened before here, so verify your new revision id against the existing set).

Also implement: classify the grant/permission error specifically (UC error names the schema — surface that), and add the frontend surface on the connection detail view showing the failure state (find the existing connection-detail component and the inventory_sync toggle in it).

input.description: Fix #1108 inconsistent paging totals
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1108. Run `gh issue view 1108` for full text. Summary: `GET /assets` has an `X-Total-Count` header (via a `TOTAL_COUNT_HEADER` constant in `backend/app/api/v1/assets.py`, already CORS-exposed) added by #925. Sibling list endpoints with the same silent-truncation defect class still lack a total:
- `GET /pipeline_runs` — has limit+offset (#928) but no total; the Results-page pipeline-runs tab does a single 200-row fetch with no "showing N of M" indication.
- `GET /incidents` — has limit+offset, no total anywhere.
- `GET /runs` — has limit only, can't even be paged.

Acceptance criteria (from the issue):

input.description: Fix #1107 tree-view walk not cancelled
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ), frontend is React + Vite + Ant Design, pnpm. Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1107. Run `gh issue view 1107` for full text. Summary: the assets tree-view's multi-page fetch (`fetchAllAssetsForTree`, and the `useAsyncData` hook it runs under) has two gaps:
1. Unmount does NOT cancel the walk. `useAsyncData` only suppresses the late `setState`, but `fetchAllAssetsForTree` keeps issuing up to 10 sequential page requests after the view unmounts (e.g. a Segmented-control toggle away mid-walk). Rapid toggling compounds this — each remount starts an independent new walk.
2. Every toggle back to the tree view re-walks the full population from scratch, even when nothing changed (a regression from when this was one shared fetch, pre-#925).

Fix direction: thread an abort signal through `useAsyncData` into the walk loop (checked per iteration, so an unmount/toggle-away stops issuing further page requests), and either lift the fetch above the toggle or cache the last complete walk keyed by a nonce (so toggling back doesn't re-walk when a completed walk already exists for the current nonce).

Acceptance criteria (from the issue, write tests for each):
- [ ] Toggling away mid-walk stops further page requests — test: mock N pages, toggle away after page 1 resolves, assert no further fetch calls happen.
- [ ] Toggling back does NOT re-fetch when a completed walk already exists for the current nonce.
- [ ] Rapid toggling produces at most one in-flight walk at a time.

Workflow:
1. `pnpm install` if needed under `frontend/`, work from there.
2. Branch: `git checkout -b fix/issue-1107-tree-walk-cancel`.
3. Find `useAsyncData` and `fetchAllAssetsForTree` (grep under `frontend/src/`), implement the abort-signal threading + walk cache.

input.description: Fix #1001 profiler sampler full download
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1001. Run `gh issue view 1001` for full text. Context: this is split out of already-merged #882, which fixed *introspection* paths (column listing, schema-drift) by routing them through a `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam in `backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py`. `profile_service._read_file_sample` was deliberately left on whole-object download. Read #882's diff/history first (`git log --all --oneline --grep=882` or search) to understand the existing `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam so you reuse it rather than inventing a new one.

Scope, per the issue's own acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Parquet sampling reads only the projected columns of the rows it needs, NOT the whole object. The issue suggests: `pq.ParquetFile(RangeReader(...)).iter_batches(batch_size=_SAMPLE_ROWS, columns=present)` reads roughly one row group's worth of the projected columns and produces the same sample.
- [ ] CSV sampling either keeps its current full sample size, OR surfaces explicitly when a bound truncated it — it must NEVER silently sample fewer rows than before (this is the #839 lesson: quietly shrinking a statistic is worse than the egress it saves — do not implement a naive fixed-size head-range for CSV, since that would silently cap the sample below `_SAMPLE_ROWS` on a wide file and change profiler output — distinct counts, top values, min/max — with no signal that it happened). If you can't safely bound CSV reads without this risk, it is acceptable to leave CSV on whole-object download for this PR and say so explicitly, since the Parquet win stands alone.
- [ ] A test asserts the BYTES READ (not just resulting stats) — a correctness-only assertion passes either way and wouldn't catch a regression back to whole-object download. Check how #882's own tests asserted this for the introspection paths and mirror that pattern (likely mocking/counting the range-read calls or byte offsets requested).

Workflow:
1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run`).
2. Branch: `git checkout -b fix/issue-1001-profiler-sampler-range-read`.
3. Implement the Parquet fix (and CSV if you can do it safely per the constraint above; otherwise state clearly why not).
4. Run Black/Ruff/mypy + relevant profiler/flatfile tests locally.
5. Commit (conventional commit, `Fixes #1001`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push, open PR (use `.github/pull_request_template.md`), milestone matching issue #1001's (`gh issue view 1001 --json milestone`).
6. Run the `/code-review` skill on your diff; fix blocking findings; file a new issue for anything deferred (e.g. if CSV stays whole-object, that's fine to note in the PR, doesn't need a new issue since the original issue itself scoped that possibility, but call it out clearly).
7. Wait for CI green; squash-merge if clean (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`).
8. Report: PR URL, merge status, what you did for CSV and why, follow-ups filed.

input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: implement GitHub issue #1193 (a small feature, not a one-liner). Run `gh issue view 1193` for full text, and read the already-merged PRs #1180 and #1192 (`gh pr view 1180`, `gh pr view 1192`) for context on the existing batch-target UI and backend support before starting.

Summary: #1180 added a Single-file / Batch-pattern mode toggle to `SuiteForm`, wiring the UI to the backend's existing `resolve_batch`/`BatchSpec` batch-target support (prefix/pattern/strategy/batch) in `backend/app/datasources/flatfile.py`. But no cheap PREVIEW path exists: `POST /suites/{id}/profile`, `GET /suites/{id}/columns`, and `POST /suites/{id}/column-policy/suggest` all accept only a literal `path`/`table` — none take `pattern`/`strategy`/`batch`/`prefix`. #1192 (per its own scoping instruction) did NOT add a new backend endpoint, and instead only shows the CONFIGURED prefix+pattern+strategy (via `summarizeTarget`), not a resolved file.

input.description: Build #1199 near-miss surfacing
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly. Also note CLAUDE.md §4/§11: never bypass the `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction, and never treat ADF/Airflow as datasources — this feature is provider-agnostic by nature, keep it that way.

Task: implement GitHub issue #1199 (a product-gap feature, needs a design pick). Run `gh issue view 1199` for full text, and read merged PR #1194 (`gh pr view 1194`) and issue #1186 for context on the existing near-miss signal.

Summary: #1194 added an ingest-time near-miss signal: when a succeeded pipeline/DAG run matches an ENABLED `trigger_binding` on `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)` but NOT on `env`, `orchestration_service._record_env_near_misses` emits a structlog warning AND upserts a deduped row in `workspace_health` (key `trigger_env_near_miss:<hash>`). That row is currently WRITE-ONLY — no API route, no frontend surface reads it. Only `psql` can see it today. This repeats the #828/#837/#1100 shape (a signal recorded but invisible in the product).

The issue gives 3 acceptance ideas to choose from at design time — pick the one that best fits existing conventions, don't try to do all three:
1. A read endpoint (e.g. `GET /admin/orchestration/near-misses` or folded into an existing admin/health surface) listing current near-miss rows decoded back to `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id, run_env, binding_env, updated_at)`. NOTE: the stored `workspace_health.key` is a HASH (chosen to fit the 64-char column against Airflow's up-to-256-char DAG ids) — so either add a sibling detail column/table to `workspace_health` holding the un-hashed tuple, or have the read path re-derive candidates by re-running `_record_env_near_misses`'s own query, filtered to recent `updated_at`. Read that function's implementation carefully before picking.
2. A badge/alert on the Suite Triggers panel (`TriggersPanel.tsx`) for a binding whose `(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)` has a recent near-miss row in a DIFFERENT env than the binding itself.
3. Fold into a future workspace-health/admin dashboard alongside the existing poll-staleness signal (`workspace_health_service.POLL_STALENESS_KEY`).

Recommended: do BOTH 1 and 2 together (the read endpoint from 1 is what 2 consumes) since that's the most complete and directly addresses "invisible except via psql" — option 3 alone would just move the same invisibility into a future dashboard that doesn't exist yet. Use your judgment; if scope creeps too large, ship option 1 alone (a working read endpoint is real product value even before the UI badge) and file the UI badge as its own follow-up issue.

Workflow:
1. `conda activate dataq` for backend (never `conda run`); `pnpm` for frontend if you touch UI.
2. Branch: `git checkout -b feature/issue-1199-near-miss-surfacing`.
3. Implement per your chosen design. Add tests: read endpoint returns current near-miss rows correctly decoded/matched; a resolved (no-longer-recurring) near-miss doesn't show as current; if you add the UI badge, test it renders when a binding has a recent mismatched-env near-miss.
4. Run Black/Ruff/mypy + backend tests, frontend lint/typecheck/tests if applicable, locally.

7. Wait for CI green; squash-merge if clean (`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`).
8. Report: PR URL, merge status, which design option(s) you chose and why, follow-ups filed.

input.description: Build #1202 custom-SQL metric_value
input.prompt:
Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ). Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge), AND note CLAUDE.md §10's critical rule: "metric_value is the SQL-aggregatable scalar a monitor measured; don't store metrics only in JSONB observed_value." Follow CLAUDE.md exactly.

Task: implement GitHub issue #1202 (needs a deliberate design decision, per the issue). Run `gh issue view 1202` for full text, and read ADR 0019 (`docs/adr/0019-*.md` — find the exact filename) for the existing custom-SQL check design, plus the already-merged severity/metric_value seam (grep `severity.extract_metric` under `backend/app/`).

Summary: a custom-SQL check (ADR 0019) produces a genuine scalar — the unexpected row count — but it lands ONLY in JSONB: `observed_value = {"observed_value": 74}`. `metric_value` stays NULL on both Snowflake and Unity Catalog. ADR 0019 §4 deliberately chose binary pass/fail for "this query should return no rows" (correct, don't change that), but the row count itself is never captured as a bandable metric, so: the per-check metric trend view (#594) has nothing to plot for custom-SQL checks, an `anomaly` monitor can't baseline against it, and "is this rule getting worse?" is unanswerable in SQL.

Scope (per the issue, this is EXACT — follow it, don't improvise beyond it):
- Populate `metric_value` from the unexpected row count in `gx_runner`/`severity.extract_metric` for `unexpected_rows_expectation`, on BOTH datasources (Snowflake and Unity Catalog) at once — a per-datasource divergence would make the same check band differently depending on where it runs. This is an ADDITIVE change in `severity.extract_metric` — ADR 0019 §Consequences already confirms "no schema change" (the `metric_value` column already exists per the Week-3 threshold migration, per CLAUDE.md §10 — do NOT add a migration).
- Decide the semantic DELIBERATELY: a raw row count is not comparable across tables of different sizes — decide whether the bandable quantity should be the raw count, or a percentage of the batch (which costs a second aggregate query). Make this decision explicitly and document your reasoning in the PR description; don't just pick silently.
- CRITICAL constraint: existing rows keep `metric_value = NULL` — do NOT backfill a guess.
- CRITICAL constraint: thresholds are already optional on a check — adding a metric must NOT turn today's binary (no-threshold) checks into something that bands unexpectedly. A check with no thresholds configured must keep resolving EXACTLY as it does today (pass/fail only, no band). Write a test specifically proving this: a no-threshold custom-SQL check with unexpected_rows > 0 still resolves as a simple fail with no severity band applied, even though `metric_value` is now populated.

Required tests: `metric_value` gets populated with the chosen semantic on both Snowflake and Unity Catalog paths (mock/fixture both); a check WITH thresholds now bands correctly against the new metric; a check WITHOUT thresholds is unaffected (see constraint above); existing/old rows with NULL `metric_value` are left alone (no backfill logic exists).

Workflow:
1. `conda activate dataq` (never `conda run`).
2. Branch: `git checkout -b feature/issue-1202-custom-sql-metric-value`.
3. Implement in `severity.extract_metric` (or wherever the ADR points) + tests as above.
4. Run Black/Ruff/mypy + relevant tests (severity, gx_runner, both datasource run-path tests) locally.
5. Commit (conventional commit — `feat:`, `Fixes #1202`, `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push, open PR (use `.github/pull_request_template.md`), milestone matching issue #1202's (`gh issue view 1202 --json milestone`), and explain your count-vs-percentage decision clearly in the PR description.

Repo: DataQ (TheurgicDuke771/DataQ), frontend is React + Vite + Ant Design, pnpm. Read CLAUDE.md in the repo root first for the mandatory per-functionality workflow (branch → implement → tests → /code-review skill → push → PR → merge). Follow it exactly.

Task: fix GitHub issue #1107. Run `gh issue view 1107` for full text. Summary: the assets tree-view's multi-page fetch (`fetchAllAssetsForTree`, and the `useAsyncData` hook it runs under) has two gaps:
1. Unmount does NOT cancel the walk. `useAsyncData` only suppresses the late `setState`, but `fetchAllAssetsForTree` keeps issuing up to 10 sequential page requests after the view unmounts (e.g. a Segmented-control toggle away mid-walk). Rapid toggling compounds this — each remount starts an independent new walk.
2. Every toggle back to the tree view re-walks the full population from scratch, even when nothing changed (a regression from when this was one shared fetch, pre-#925).

Fix direction: thread an abort signal through `useAsyncData` into the walk loop (checked per iteration, so an unmount/toggle-away stops issuing further page requests), and either lift the fetch above the toggle or cache the last complete walk keyed by a nonce (so toggling back doesn't re-walk when a completed walk already exists for the current nonce).

Acceptance criteria (from the issue, write tests for each):
- [ ] Toggling away mid-walk stops further page requests — test: mock N pages, toggle away after page 1 resolves, assert no further fetch calls happen.
- [ ] Toggling back does NOT re-fetch when a completed walk already exists for the current nonce.
- [ ] Rapid toggling produces at most one in-flight walk at a time.

<summary>Agent "Verify DB connect_timeout gap findings" finished</summary>
<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Verification results

### Candidate 1 — psycopg2 `connect_timeout` doesn't bound pooled/reused connections

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

The mechanics check out against documented behavior, and this doesn't require a live network-partition test to establish — it follows deterministically from how libpq and SQLAlchemy's pool are specified to work:

- **psycopg2/libpq `connect_timeout`** is a libpq connection parameter. It only bounds the time from socket-open through the connection reaching `CONNECTION_OK` (TCP handshake + auth). Once `create_engine()`'s `connect_args` produces a live DBAPI connection and it's returned to the pool, `connect_timeout` has no further effect on that connection — it is not re-applied to reads/writes on an already-open socket, and psycopg2 does not translate it into an ongoing `SO_RCVTIMEO`/socket read timeout.
- **`pool_pre_ping=True`** in SQLAlchemy runs `dialect.do_ping(dbapi_connection)` on checkout — for the psycopg2/postgres dialect this executes a cursor query (effectively `SELECT 1`) on the **existing pooled DBAPI connection object**. This is not a call to `connect()`, so `connect_timeout` is architecturally out of scope for it.
- No `statement_timeout` GUC is set (the file's own comment explicitly says this is deliberate, to not cap legitimate long-running GX queries), and no psycopg2 socket-level keepalive args (`keepalives`, `keepalives_idle`, `keepalives_interval`, `keepalives_count`) are set either — those would be the mechanism that lets the OS detect a silently-dead peer on an idle/in-use socket. Their absence corroborates the gap.
- On a routing-level partition with no RST/ICMP-unreachable, a blocking read on that socket is bounded only by the OS's TCP retransmission timeout (Linux default `tcp_retries2` ≈ 15, commonly 13–30 min depending on RTT) — large and effectively "the same order of unboundedness" the PR set out to eliminate, not the ~10s the fix advertises.

So the reasoning is sound: the fix genuinely narrows the **first-connect** case (a DB that's unreachable *before* the app ever talks to it — cold start, or a connection recycled after `pool_pre_ping` detects and discards a dead one) but does **not** protect a connection that was healthy, is sitting checked-out or idle in the pool, and goes silent mid-life. The file's own comment ("a dead DB fails fast and loudly instead of hanging every caller") overclaims relative to that scope — "every caller" is true only for callers needing a *new* connection, not ones reusing a pooled one. For the specific #1052 staleness-loop shutdown scenario named in the PR, if the partition happens after the loop's connection is already established and pooled, the graceful-shutdown await can still hang for OS-timeout-scale duration.

### Candidate 2 — `backend/alembic/env.py` still has the same unbounded-connect gap

**Verdict: CONFIRMED**

Read the file directly:

```python
# backend/alembic/env.py, lines 48-54
def run_migrations_online() -> None:
    connectable = engine_from_config(
        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
        connect_args={"options": f"-c lock_timeout={int(_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS)}"},
    )
```

This engine sets `lock_timeout` (15s) via the `options` GUC string but has no `connect_timeout` key at all. This is exactly the bug class PR #1216 fixes for the app engine (`backend/app/db/session.py`), left open in the migration path. It's a real, live gap: the `dataq-app-migrate` ACA job runs `alembic upgrade head` before the api/worker roll, per the deploy runbook — if Postgres is unreachable at that moment (network partition, DNS/host issue, etc.), the migrate job's initial `connect()` would hang on the OS/driver default, not the intended 10s, potentially stalling the whole Deploy workflow run rather than failing fast.

Worth flagging as a followup: it's the same author intent ("fail fast and loudly instead of hanging") not yet applied to the second of the two hand-rolled engines in the codebase. Per CLAUDE.md's finding-disposition rule, this shouldn't be left as a review comment only — it should be fixed in the same PR if trivial (add `connect_args={"options": ..., "connect_timeout": N}` mirroring `_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, using the migration's own constant or importing the app one) or filed as a `gh issue` if deferred.

## Suggested action for the PR review

- Candidate 1: comment on the PR that the docstring/PR-description claim ("fails fast... instead of hanging every caller") should be scoped down to "new connections" — either soften the claim, or extend the fix with TCP keepalive `connect_args` (`keepalives=1, keepalives_idle=…, keepalives_interval=…, keepalives_count=…`) if the intent is to also bound mid-life partition detection on pooled connections. At minimum this is worth a filed follow-up issue per the "fixed or filed" rule, not silently accepted as full coverage.
- Candidate 2: recommend adding `connect_timeout` to `backend/alembic/env.py`'s `connect_args` in this PR (small, same-shaped fix, arguably "one functionality" since it's the identical defect class) — or file a GitHub issue referencing #1216 if the PR author wants to keep scope narrow.</result>

- **No-thresholds binary fallback (ADR 0005, `derive_status`, untouched by this diff) still holds**: populating `metric_value` for custom-SQL checks does not change `derive_status`'s `no_thresholds` short-circuit, verified by `test_resolve_status_custom_sql_without_thresholds_stays_binary_despite_populated_metric`.

The core design question for this PR (raw row-count vs. percentage-of-batch as the bandable metric) was explicitly raised as an open decision in **issue #1202** itself, which was split out of the **PR #1201** review ("fix(datasources): make custom SQL actually run on Unity Catalog", merged 2026-08-08). #1202's body says:

PR #1223 addresses this head-on — its new module docstring in `severity.py` explicitly cites #1202 and justifies choosing raw count over percentage (no second aggregate query needed since `severity.py` is pure/no-DB-access, and the metric is only ever compared per-check against its own history, never cross-check, so cross-table comparability doesn't matter). This looks like a deliberate, documented resolution of the exact concern the prior review flagged — not an oversight.

**Related but NOT applicable to this PR — verified benign:**

PR #1201's review also filed **issue #1203** (a SQL-batch `StatementError` can leak a target cell value into `observed_value` on **errored** checks, bypassing the column-redaction policy). I checked whether this interacts with #1223's new `extract_metric` fallback: it does not — `resolve_status` (in `severity.py`) short-circuits on `outcome.errored` and returns `("error", None)` **before** `extract_metric` is ever called, so the errored/leaked-cell path never reaches the new custom-SQL row-count branch. Additionally, `extract_metric` wraps the `Decimal(str(raw))` conversion in a `try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, TypeError)` that safely falls back to `None`, so even a non-numeric `observed_value` couldn't crash it. No action needed for #1223.

- PR #1117/#1119 (anomaly monitor kind + authoring UI) — findings were UI form-validation bugs (`min_points` bounds, zero-threshold client validation), not about what counts as a valid bandable metric.

**Bottom line:** No unresolved or forgotten caveats from prior PRs apply to PR #1223's approach. This is a substantive batch of findings on #1104's PR (#1227) — worth flagging clearly:

1. **Unguarded `session.commit()` inside the `except` block** with no nested try/except — if that bookkeeping commit itself fails, it aborts the entire nightly sweep for every remaining connection, not just the one that failed. Same risk on the success-path `else` branch's commit.
2. **Missing row-lock on `inventory_sync_failing_since`** — plain read-modify-write with no `with_for_update()`, a lost-update race under concurrent sweeps. The codebase has an *exact* precedent for this (`orchestration_service.record_poll_failure`'s `consecutive_poll_failures`) that explicitly uses row-locking for this reason — this PR didn't follow it.
3. **Reading stale/expired ORM attributes after `session.rollback()`** without re-fetching — `record_poll_failure`'s own docstring documents this exact hazard in this exact codebase and re-fetches deliberately; this PR reuses the stale instance instead, risking `ObjectDeletedError` if the connection was deleted concurrently.

These aren't nitpicks — they're real robustness gaps against documented precedent in the same codebase. Letting the #1104 agent work through them; I'll check in if it looks like it's heading toward merging without addressing the two race/failure-cascade issues.

<result>Confirmed there is a global `DataQError` → HTTP-response mapping, which is exactly why the sibling endpoints (dry-run, profile) never need a router-level `try/except` at all — the service layer raises typed `DataQError` subclasses and FastAPI's handler does the rest.

## Findings

**Angle 1 — Altitude**

1. `_FLATFILE_TYPES` in `backend/app/services/run_target.py` (lines 128–131, 158–162) is dead-weight duplication, not a justified special case. Traced the actual call path: `preview_batch` → `resolve_target` → `resolve_target_shape` (`backend/app/datasources/registry.py:357`) → `_TARGET_RESOLVERS`. That registry has no entry for `adf`/`airflow` (raises `TargetShapeError("...has no run path...")`) and its `snowflake`/`unity_catalog`/`iceberg` resolvers all call `_require(target, "table", conn_type)`, which already raises `TargetShapeError` because a batch-shaped `{pattern, strategy, prefix}` dict has no `table` key. So for every connection type the guard rejects, `resolve_target` — called two lines later in the very same function — would already raise the equivalent `SuiteTargetInvalidError`. The guard only changes the error string, not the outcome. Its own comment ("duplicated ... rather than imported so this module's write-time validation path stays GX-free") is also empirically false: `run_target.py:43` already does `from backend.app.datasources.registry import resolve_target_shape` unconditionally at module load, and `registry.py` already does `from backend.app.datasources.flatfile import build_flatfile_runner` unconditionally at module load, and `flatfile.py:39` does `import great_expectations as gx` at module load — so importing `run_target` (which `suite_service`'s write path already does) has been loading GX transitively all along, pre-existing this PR. The stated GX-avoidance rationale doesn't hold, so there's no justification left for hand-duplicating the type set instead of calling `resolve_target_shape` directly and mapping its (already-correct) `TargetShapeError`/`SuiteTargetInvalidError`.

2. The three new error classes (`BatchPreviewNoDataError`, `BatchPreviewInvalidError`, `BatchPreviewFailedError`) and their try/except mapping live in the **router** (`backend/app/api/v1/suites.py:517–529, 561–589`). Every sibling no-persistence preview endpoint does the opposite: `dry_run_check` (`backend/app/api/v1/checks.py:452`) has zero try/except and is a pure pass-through to `dryrun_service.dry_run_check`, whose own module (`backend/app/services/dryrun_service.py:51,56,...`) defines `DryRunUnsupportedError`/`DryRunNoDataError`/`DryRunFailedError` and does the identical `BatchNotFoundError→422 / DataQError passthrough / Exception→502 w/ classify_failure_reason` translation internally. `profile_columns` (`suites.py:426`) is the same: `ProfileUnsupportedError` etc. live in `profile_service.py:91–113`, and the router has no try/except at all. Batch-preview inverts this: `run_target.preview_batch` leaks raw `flatfile.BatchNotFoundError`/`BatchListingTooLargeError` (both bare `ValueError`s) up to the router, which then has to know the flatfile module's exception types to translate them. This is an inconsistency in where error taxonomy is owned — a future service-layer caller of `preview_batch` (not the HTTP router) gets undifferentiated `ValueError`s instead of typed `DataQError`s the way every other service in this codebase behaves.

No CLAUDE.md-quotable violations found (angle 2) — the PR correctly keeps ADF/Airflow out of `_FLATFILE_TYPES`/the registry, touches no migration, and adds no tracked secret.
